classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1): A machine part card carries four rule-bearing regions — name, roll conditions (damage requirements), a cycle track the part's yellow HP die moves down, and cycle icon effects triggered when the die lands on an icon.
classifications.reason: Every cited fact passed grounding validation (verbatim-traceable to both enumerator lists).

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1): Destroying a part converts its yellow HP die into a player die, so the player's pool grows as parts are destroyed, capped at 10 dice (5 black + 5 yellow).
classifications.reason: Every cited fact passed grounding validation (verbatim-traceable to both enumerator lists).

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1): Roll conditions on machine part cards are expressed with a compact symbol language: "?" means any value, an explicit pip face means an exact value, "/" means either-or, "+" and "=" express arithmetic/equality relations across dice, and ">" expresses a comparison.
classifications.reason: No grounded fact corroborates this Derived line, and the rulebook source is quote-verified, so the gap is reported rather than downgraded.

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1): The game is a repeating two-phase loop (Phase I player dice allocation, Phase II machine phase) that ends only in a win (Doom Core destroyed) or a loss (player destroyed).
classifications.reason: Every cited fact passed grounding validation (verbatim-traceable to both enumerator lists).

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1): The player's dice pool ranges from 5 dice (5 black) up to 10 dice (5 black + 5 yellow), and all available dice are re-rolled at the start of each turn.
classifications.reason: Reconciler claimed "corroborated-by-composition" citing a composed-fact id that either does not exist or was verified against different Derived-line text — downgraded rather than trusted.

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1, p.2): The machine deck for a normal game is 9 face-up-drawable machine part cards stacked on top of the face-down Doom Core, so the Doom Core is the final card of the deck. Of those 9, the top 3 are immediately revealed in step 5, leaving 6 face down above the Doom Core.
classifications.reason: Reconciler claimed "corroborated-by-composition" citing a composed-fact id that either does not exist or was verified against different Derived-line text — downgraded rather than trusted.

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1): The Doom Machine tracking card has two tracks — Sentience (yellow) and Power (black) — each starting at zero.
classifications.reason: Every cited fact passed grounding validation (verbatim-traceable to both enumerator lists).
Every cited fact passed grounding validation (verbatim-traceable to both enumerator lists).

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.2): These icons appear on machine part cycle tracks; a part's die landing on an icon during the machine phase triggers the corresponding effect (see Phase II, p.2 panel -8-).
classifications.reason: No grounded fact corroborates this Derived line, and the rulebook source is quote-verified, so the gap is reported rather than downgraded.

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1, p.2): Hard Mode changes exactly three things: the full card pool is used instead of a reduced one, the Player HP card's B side offers one fewer shield slot / re-roll slot / +-modifier slot, and the per-turn shield dice limit drops from 4 to 3.
classifications.reason: Every cited fact passed grounding validation (verbatim-traceable to both enumerator lists).

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.1, p.2): Each machine phase, every part in play advances one step on its own cycle track (wrapping back to the start if it would land on a dead space), and then one new part card joins the line from the left, up to a maximum of 10 parts.
classifications.reason: Every cited fact passed grounding validation (verbatim-traceable to both enumerator lists).

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.2): Utility slots (+/- modifier slots and re-roll slots) live on the Player HP tracking card, since Hard Mode removes a shield slot, a re-roll slot, and a roll modifier slot by flipping that card (see p.1, panel -11-).
classifications.reason: No grounded fact corroborates this Derived line, and the rulebook source is quote-verified, so the gap is reported rather than downgraded.

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.2): Shield strength is consumed by reducing the face values of the dice sitting in shield slots; once a shield die's value is exhausted it goes to the spent dice pile.
classifications.reason: Every cited fact passed grounding validation (verbatim-traceable to both enumerator lists).

classifications.derivedLineText: Derived (p.2): The only win condition is destroying the Doom Core; the only loss condition is Player HP reaching zero.
classifications.reason: Every cited fact passed grounding validation (verbatim-traceable to both enumerator lists).
